title: Ugali with Sukuma Wiki Greens
summary: White maize meal cooked and pressed into a firm dome, served with greens cooked with onion, tomato and ginger.

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
fine sea salt or table salt
collard greens or kale, stems removed, cut into thin ribbons

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the maize meal into the 700 ml cold water in the saucepan until smooth.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Set over medium heat, pour 240 ml of the extra water around the edge, part-cover and cook 6-8 min until bubbling; stir hard 2 min to smooth out.

steps.title: Firm
steps.text: Keep folding and pressing the mixture against the pan over medium-low heat 15-20 min, adding a splash of the remaining water only if it is too stiff, until it pulls cleanly from the sides and smells toasty; cover off the heat 5 min.

steps.title: Greens
steps.text: Meanwhile, fry the onion in the oil 5 min, add the tomatoes, ginger and salt for 5 min, then the greens for 8-10 min until tender.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Turn the ugali into a wet bowl, invert onto a plate to make a dome and serve with the greens.

tips: Use a sturdy wooden spoon; the ugali gets very stiff.
Wet the bowl so the dome turns out cleanly.
Eat by pinching off pieces of ugali to scoop the greens.
storage: Best fresh; keep the greens covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
